title.narrative: COVID-19: Responsive COVID-19 Vaccines for Recovery Project under the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility

description.narrative: The project will provide the Government of Bangladesh with timely financing for procuring safe and effective vaccines against the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) based on an agreed list of eligible expenditures. It will utilize the rapid response component (RRC) under the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility (APVAX). Ongoing technical assistance (TA) will help strengthen the vaccine delivery system. The project is aligned with three operational priorities of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) Strategy 2030: (i) addressing remaining poverty and reducing inequalities, (ii) accelerating progress in gender equality, and (iii) fostering regional cooperation and integration. It is also aligned with ADB's country partnership strategy for Bangladesh, 2016-2020 in the priority areas of improving human capital and health care, and promoting gender equality

Output: Safe and effective COVID-19 vaccines delivered Indicator: 3,000 health staff trained in online registration and generating vaccination cards in rural and hard-to-reach areas (50% women) Achievement: 3000 Progress/Status: DGHS conducted the training activities before the initiation of the project tenure and through EPI & MIS program. Output: Safe and effective COVID-19 vaccines delivered Indicator: Up to 44.7 million doses of COVID-19 and routine vaccines procured and delivered to the country Achievement: 58 Progress/Status: Over 58 million doses of Sinopharm vaccine financed by ADB (6 million in contract no. 063 and 52.5 million in contract no. 131) have been delivered by MNCH, DGHS. Up to 20.13 million Bangladeshis (11.6% of the total population) vaccinated against COVID-19 and routine vaccines, based on government's vaccine allocation plan Achievement: 11.6 Progress/Status: As of 30 Sep 2025, a total of 366,725,205 (about 366 million doses) vaccine doses have been administered including doses under APVAX facility. Among the doses 150,922,861 (male: 75,235,432; female: 75,687,429) were first dose, 142,193,280 (male: 70,557,366; female: 71,635,803) second dose, 68,558,519 (male: 33,924,467; female: 34,634,052) amounts of third dose & 5,050,545 (male: 2,818,043; female: 2,232,502) of fourth dose were given. It is to be mentioned that, all vaccines under APVAX facility have been inoculated during first & second dose. Data Source: DGHS Hospital Information Management System COVID-19 vaccination coverage weekly report; COVID-19 vaccination dashboard; and WHO and UNICEF immunization estimates to supplement
